witness.statement: For every prime p <= 1000000, with n = p - 1: (i) m_n = p, i.e. p is the least positive integer m with n | phi(m); (ii) p_n = p, i.e. p is the least prime congruent to 1 mod n.
witness.reasoning_checked: m <= n implies phi(m) <= m - 1 < n, so the least witness m_n for n = p-1 is exactly p; every prime congruent to 1 mod (p-1) is at least p, and p qualifies, so p_n = p. Verifier inversion: a violation of (i) exists iff some m < BOUND has a divisor d of phi(m) with d+1 prime, d+1 <= BOUND, and m < d+1.

run.detail: AssertionError: smaller witness m=1 for n=1

claim: A clean exit 0 certifies, by exact integer arithmetic, no floats, no I/O, no network, deterministic and fail-closed (any violated expectation raises and aborts nonzero), that for every prime p <= 10^6 the least m with (p-1) | phi(m) is exactly p and the least prime congruent to 1 mod (p-1) is exactly p, i.e. m_n = p = p_n at n = p-1 throughout the instance range of standing lemma L1.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
